articles.title: Who is Uncle Dennis? What to know about Kawhi Leonard's adviser Dennis Robertson and his role in NBA's investigation
articles.summary: Dennis Robertson was punished by the NBA for his actions during the Aspiration scandal.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Clippers star Kawhi Leonard was reportedly paid $28 million by a company funded by team owner Steve Ballmer that helped the Clippers evade the NBA salary cap, according to a report by Pablo Torre in 2025.

Nearly a full year after the NBA launched a formal investigation into the matter, it issued its findings Wednesday, docking the Clippers five first-round picks, fining Ballmer $30 million and fining Leonard $700,000, among other penalties.

On his show, " Pablo Torre Finds Out ," Torre detailed a now-bankrupt company named Aspiration, which paid $28 million to KL2 Aspire LLC, a company owned by Leonard. Clauses in the contract between Aspiration and Leonard's company indicated Leonard wouldn't have to do anything other than be a member of the Clippers to receive that money. One employee spoke with Torre, saying they were told Leonard's contract was a way to "circumvent the salary cap."

One key figure referenced several times during Torre's investigation — and in the NBA's ruling Wednesday — was Dennis Robertson, otherwise known as Uncle Dennis. Robertson, who was also subject to an NBA investigation in 2019, reportedly also played a role in the Aspiration scandal.

Who is Uncle Dennis, and what happened with his previous investigation? And how did the NBA come down on Uncle Dennis on Wednesday? Here's what you need to know about Robertson and his relationship with Leonard.

Uncle Dennis is Dennis Robertson. Some publications have referred to Robertson as Leonard's adviser. Robertson is also Leonard's actual uncle.

What is Uncle Dennis' role in the Aspiration scandal?

Robertson's name was listed on a contract between Aspiration and KL2 Aspire LLC. The specific sentence pertaining to Robertson specified that all "communication required or permitted under this Agreement" be sent to Robertson. In addition to that, Robertson was listed in the contract as Leonard's "designated representative."

The former Aspiration employee who spoke with Torre mentioned that a top priority at Aspiration was making sure Leonard's contract got paid, and that Robertson called to demand payment when the company got in a rough financial situation.

Robertson's name being on legal documents proves he had at least some involvement in the two companies involved in the alleged scandal. While Robertson's name being on documents didn't necessarily prove anything, it gave the NBA evidence to reopen its 2019 investigation into Leonard's free agency.

Why was Uncle Dennis investigated by the NBA in 2019?

Robertson was at the center of an NBA investigation focusing on whether he asked teams for impermissible benefits during Leonard's free-agent process. Robertson was accused of asking for part ownership of the team, a private plane to be available to Leonard at all times and a guaranteed amount of off-court endorsement money that could be guaranteed to Leonard if he played for that team, per The Athletic.

Robertson was accused of making those asks to both the Los Angeles Lakers and Toronto Raptors. Lakers owner Jeanie Buss reportedly informed Robertson at the time that those types of benefits were illegal.

What did the NBA find in its 2019 investigation of Uncle Dennis?

After looking into the situation, the league claimed it had no evidence that the Clippers granted illegal benefits to Leonard during his free agency. The team, Leonard and Robertson did not face punishment as a result of the investigation.

The league, however, threatened it could reopen its investigation into the situation if new evidence were presented. At the time, a source told Sam Amick of The Athletic that NBA commissioner Adam Silver considered the issue "a cardinal sin of the NBA."

How did the NBA respond to the 2019 investigation?

In September 2019, the league introduced harsher penalties for free-agent tampering. The NBA doubled fines for tampering and passed a rule allowing Silver to take phones and laptops away from team executives to check for impermissible communication.

That wasn't necessarily a direct response to Leonard's situation. Tampering allegations surrounded a number of players around the league for multiple years before the league finally cracked down on the practice in 2019.

How did the Clippers respond to the Aspiration investigation?

Throughout the entire investigation process, both the Clippers and Ballmer maintained their innocence. Once the league dropped the hammer on the franchise Wednesday, the Clippers put out a statement announcing the franchise would fight back against the NBA's "witch hunt."

How did the NBA first respond to the Aspiration allegations?

The NBA quickly launched a new investigation into the situation. Other than a spare comment here and there, the league mostly remained quiet about the status of that investigation, instead waiting until Wednesday to finally reveal its punishment.

How was Uncle Dennis punished after NBA's second investigation?

Robertson was banned by the NBA for five years for improperly soliciting off-court income opportunities for Leonard, the league revealed.

"Mr. Robertson is banned from conducting business or otherwise engaging with NBA teams and their affiliates on behalf of or with respect to any player, employee, or other league or team personnel for a period of five years."

In its bullet points explaining its decision to punish the Clippers, the NBA said the team's failure to report that Robertson was seeking improper benefits for Leonard was one of the factors that led to the league's punishment.

articles.title: Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu mansion listed for $48 million after massive makeover, 23 years after NBA legend bought the Pacific Coast Highway estate for $6.4 million
articles.summary: News News: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu property is back on the market for $48 million, more than two decades after he purchased the prime Pacific Co.
articles.body: NBA legend Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu property is back on the market for $48 million, more than two decades after he purchased the prime Pacific Coast Highway estate for $6.4 million. The sprawling property, which Garnett acquired in 2003 during his Minnesota Timberwolves career, has since undergone a major transformation and is now being offered as a completed luxury residence.According to property records cited by Mansion Global, Garnett purchased the Malibu estate in 2003. The property overlooks the Pacific Ocean and sits directly above Escondido Beach, spanning nearly seven acres across three parcels.Kevin Garnett bought the Malibu property for $6.4 million in 2003After purchasing the property, Garnett demolished the existing Mediterranean-style home and began developing a custom mansion. However, the project remained unfinished during his ownership.Garnett eventually sold the partially completed property in 2021 for $16 million to developer Ando Hacopian of Hacopian Design & Development Group. The transaction later became the subject of a legal dispute.As reported by The Real Deal, Garnett filed a lawsuit against Hacopian alleging fraud and subsequently sued the title and escrow companies involved in the transaction. Hacopian responded with a countersuit.The deal ultimately fell apart, and in 2022, Vladimir Valsky, CEO of VIG Private Lending and the senior lender involved in the transaction, took control of the property.From unfinished mansion to $48 million luxury estateRather than quickly sell the partially completed residence, Valsky decided to complete and significantly upgrade the property. He hired Swiss architect Roger Kurath to redesign and finish the home.“We acquired the property partially completed and saw the opportunity to finish the home the way a residence of this caliber demands,” Valsky said, according to Mansion Global.Kurath, who had not worked with Garnett on the original project, described the renovation as an extensive overhaul. “We took it down to the studs,” he said.The property has now been completed and christened “Vela”. It is being jointly listed by Chris Cortazzo of Compass and Aaron Kirman and Tomer Fridman of Christie’s International Real Estate Southern California.Inside Kevin Garnett’s former Malibu estateThe completed home spans approximately 11,000 square feet across three levels and features six bedrooms and eight bathrooms. The residence is set behind a long gated driveway off Pacific Coast Highway and offers sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean.The estate includes expansive entertaining spaces, a movie theatre, gym, wine cellar and a detached structure that can be used as a yoga studio. The resort-style grounds feature an infinity pool, pickleball court and approximately 50 avocado trees.One of the three parcels is also vacant and has its own address, giving the future owner the option of developing an additional substantial residence on the property.Listing agent Chris Cortazzo told Mansion Global that the additional parcel gives buyers the flexibility to expand the estate in the future.Kevin Garnett’s career earnings and life after the NBAWidely regarded as one of the greatest power forwards in NBA history, Garnett spent 21 seasons in the league and earned approximately $334 million in career salary. He retired in 2016 after returning to the Minnesota Timberwolves, the franchise where he established himself as one of the NBA’s most dominant stars.Since retiring from basketball, Garnett has remained active in the entertainment and sports industries. He operates production company Content Cartel Studios and cohosts the sports podcast ‘KG Certified’ with former teammate Paul Pierce.His legacy with the Timberwolves is also set to receive another major honour, with the franchise scheduled to retire his iconic No. 21 jersey in early 2027.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Andrew Wiggins Talks Klay Thompson Reunion on Heat After Winning Title with Warriors, 'He's 1-of-1'
articles.summary: Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson won a title together with the Golden State Warriors, and they'll now team up in Miami with the Heat.
articles.body:
Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson won a title together with the Golden State Warriors, and they'll now team up in Miami with the Heat.

Ahead of their reunion season, Wiggins had high praise for the legendary sharpshooter.

"He's one of the most competitive people I played with," Wiggins said. "To have him on the squad is going to be amazing. He's going to fill the locker room with joy... He's one of one. He brings that championship mentality to the team and this is a year that we can do something special and he's someone that can be a big part of it."

After the Heat landed Giannis Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster trade earlier this summer, the team was still in desperate need of some shooting. With not much cap space to work with, Miami managed to bring in one of the best shooters of all time after he agreed to a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks.

Now, the Heat have a complete roster with Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in the paint and Thompson and Wiggins on the wing. Whether Miami has enough to compete in a stacked Eastern Conference remains to be seen.

articles.title: New Kawhi Leonard Rumors on Raptors Contract Extension After Clippers Investigation Punishment
articles.summary: While the NBA announced significant penalties for both the Los Angeles Clippers and Kawhi Leonard on Wednesday, the team reportedly still plans on trading the seven-time All-Star to the Toronto Raptors.
articles.body:
While the NBA announced significant penalties for both the Los Angeles Clippers and Kawhi Leonard on Wednesday, the team reportedly still plans on trading the seven-time All-Star to the Toronto Raptors.

And the Raptors reportedly plan on making sure he is there for the foreseeable future.

"As of right now, both sides—the Clippers and Raptors—are moving forward as if the trade is going to happen," ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . "… Both sides have already spoken Wednesday night and have the intention of moving forward here with this trade.

"... The expectation is there will be an extension here to come with Kawhi Leonard."

Leonard issued a statement after the NBA announced its punishments that ended by saying, "As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate."

It would be a return to the Raptors for the 35-year-old.

He led the franchise to its only championship during his one previous season in 2018-19 and was the NBA Finals MVP from the win over the Golden State Warriors. He left to join the Clippers after that title, but the two teams agreed to a trade this past offseason that was paused while the investigation was ongoing.

The trade initially sent Leonard to Toronto for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, second-round picks in 2030 and 2033, and rights to a first-round pick swap in 2027.

An extension with Leonard would be a logical next step for the Raptors considering the 2026-27 campaign is set to be the final one on his deal.

Such a trade would also help the Clippers get some draft capital back in return after the NBA stripped them of five first-round draft picks (2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033) as part of its punishment for "a pattern of misconduct and multiple significant rules violations" that included "violating the salary cap circumvention rules contained in the league's Collective Bargaining Agreement."

Leonard was fined $700,000, while the Clippers were fined $30 million. What's more, Clippers governor Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year from all league and team activities.

Notably, the Clippers issued a statement in response that said they rejected the league's findings and planned on challenging them.

articles.title: Steve Ballmer got off light while the Clippers will pay for years
articles.summary: Steve Ballmer deserved a much more creative monetary penalty from the NBA.
articles.body:
The NBA announced the punishment for Steve Ballmer and the Los Angeles Clippers for circumventing the salary cap on Wednesday. The team was fined $30 million and docked five first-round draft picks. Meanwhile, owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for a year.

It was both eye-popping and underwhelming. After reading the report from Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, even Pablo Torre briefly wondered if the league might make Ballmer sell , but that doesn't feel right. You want an owner like Ballmer. He just spent billions building his own stadium. He is willing to do whatever he possibly can to win. He's enthusiastic and cares about the team. In this case, it ended up hurting the team, but he was trying to win a title.

Kawhi on a basketball court is worth every penny the Clippers paid him. Not just in salary, but in every secret no-show deal. And then some. We all know his resume. He's an All-NBA player. He has won titles with multiple teams and is one of the best defenders the NBA has ever seen. Last season, at age 34, he played 32 minutes in 65 games and averaged 27.9 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and 1.9 steals a game. He finished seventh in MVP voting. In seven seasons, things just didn't work out, mostly because of injuries.

Jan 5, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer (left) with mascot Chuck the Condor after the game against the Golden State Warriors at Intuit Dome. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Combine that with all the team-building mistakes, and they really got nothing but a PR nightmare. The Clippers traded away a future MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. And they lost all those picks getting Paul George so that Leonard would sign in the first place. That's a steep basketball price.

And from a basketball sense, there aren't any real victims here. Some teams were wronged, but none who were hurt. The Clippers actually saved them from a number of disappointing years of their own. They would have been the ones paying Kawhi a huge salary to not finish seasons. They would have had to deal with the annoyance of Uncle Dennis off the court. When you look at it that way, the Clippers actually saved the Lakers or Raptors or whoever else wanted him back in 2019 from a huge headache.

So the franchise and the fans have been through enough. Especially the fans, who may have been rooting for the team during the Donald Sterling era. For the longest time, this was considered one of sports' cursed franchises. Now they're back in another bad spot, which does suck for anyone who buys tickets.

REDMOND, WASHINGTON – APRIL 4: Former Microsoft CEOs Bill Gates, left, and Steve Ballmer, center, pose for photos with CEO Satya Nadella during an event celebrating the 50th Anniversary of Microsoft on April 4, 2025 in Redmond, Washington. Microsoft also highlighted updates in Copilot, the company's AI tool. (Photo by Stephen Brashear/Getty Images) Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Didn't Steve Ballmer get off kind of light? For the purposes of this article, it sure seems like it! We know he's not allowed at the Intuit Dome this season, but his house probably has a sick Halo screen TV in a living room that's bigger than your whole house. With that and a League Pass subscription, there are worse setups to watch the upcoming season.

Sure, he has to pay a $30,000,000 fine, but that doesn't seem like much punishment for Steve Ballmer. According to Forbes he's worth over $150 billion, and according to math, that's less than two-thousandths of a percent of his current net worth.

No, seriously. Go do the math yourself if you have a calculator that can handle that many zeroes.

All things considered, the fine really should have been steeper. Since the wronged parties are the other teams, what if the punishment for Steve Ballmer had to pay all their salaries this year? The cap is set at just under $170 million this season. Multiply that by the other 29 franchises, and it comes out to $4.93 billion. Still just a drop in the bucket for Baller, but maybe a fair valuation for a full small-market franchise is a bit much. Even if he is one of the 10 richest people in the world.

So what's a fair compromise between $30 million and $4.93 billion?

Sep 30, 2024; Inglewood, CA, USA; Los Angeles Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard (2) talks with team owner Steve Ballmer during media day at Intuit Dome. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

That's the name of the trope where you give someone so much of something they want that they learn their lesson and don't want it anymore. Like making someone smoke a whole pack of cigarettes so they don't ever want to smoke again. Or in this case, making the person pay Kawhi Leonard's salary while he plays elsewhere.

That's right. It's all he's wanted to do over the last seven years so let him keep doing it. Let Ballmer pay Kawhi's salary in perpetuity. As long as he's on an NBA team, Ballmer should be forced to pick up the tab. For years he's found creative ways to get money to Leonard. Let him keep doing it. This time he can divert the checks through the league office.

Leonard's salary this season is $50.3 million. The Raptors just traded for him and he wants to be there so you have to assume there's an extension coming. Maybe it counts against the Raptors' cap total. Maybe not. But let Ballmer pay it. A complicated scheme deserves a complicated punishment.

Leonard just turned 35. He'll retire long before the Clippers make another first round pick, but he'll play long enough to remind Ballmer of his transgressions for a long, long time. Especially if he keeps signing those checks.

articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026: How to watch Team USA vs. China, where to stream, schedule and more
articles.summary: How to watch the US play China at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup.
articles.body:
The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup begins this week and runs through September 13, and Team USA will begin its campaign for a twelfth championship title on Friday when the U.S. faces China in its first game of the group stage. This year's tournament takes place in Germany, so if you want to watch the USA vs. China game live, it'll be airing early ; tipoff is at 8:15 a.m. ET.

Every game of the FIBA Women's World Cup will be available to stream in the U.S. via Courtside 1891 (which can be subscribed to through DAZN) and HBO Max . You can also tune in to this game and every other Team USA game on truTV and/or TNT, which will also stream on HBO Max and live TV streaming platforms such as YouTube TV and DirecTV.

Here's what to know about how to catch Team USA vs. China at this year's FIBA World Cup.

How to watch the Team USA vs. China game at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup:

Streaming: Courtside 1891 via DAZN, HBO Max, YouTube TV and more

When is the USA vs. China game at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup?

The U.S. team plays China at the FIBA Women's basketball World Cup on Friday, Sept. 4 at 8:15 a.m. ET.

What channel is the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup on?

Team USA vs. China will air on TNT this Friday.

Where to watch the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup without cable:

In the U.S., every game of the FIBA Women's World Cup will stream on Courtside 1891, which is available through DAZN, as well as on HBO Max. Friday's game between the U.S. and China can also be streamed through live TV services like YouTube TV and DirecTV .

Which teams made it in to the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup?

articles.title: Clippers-Kawhi Leonard investigation details: What to know about the NBA's historic punishment and what comes next
articles.summary: Here are the key details about the investigation, the NBA's punishment and what comes next for the Clippers, Ballmer and Leonard.
articles.body:
After completing a nearly year-long investigation into the relationship between the Los Angeles Clippers, their owner and governor Steve Ballmer, star forward Kawhi Leonard and various business partners, the NBA handed down the most damaging punishment for a team in league history .

A 35-page report from the investigatory law firm of Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz revealed a lot about the Clippers' dealings with Leonard and also raised additional questions.

Here are the key details about the investigation, the NBA's punishment and what comes next for the Clippers, Ballmer and Leonard.

What did the Clippers and Leonard do to get in trouble?

A lot, apparently. In simplest terms, the NBA says its investigation (after Pablo Torre's initial investigation) revealed evidence the Clippers circumvented the league's salary cap to help ensure Leonard received additional compensation — like a lot of additional compensation — outside of his salary. League rules put a limit on what teams can pay players. Going beyond that, whether it's from the franchise directly or funneled via the team through sponsors or other businesses, is one of the most serious violations of NBA governance.

There had been reports for years that Leonard's uncle and business adviser, Dennis Robertson, sought extra benefits and money from teams pursuing Leonard in free agency in 2019. The NBA investigated those claims and said it did not uncover evidence of any violations but would keep the case open.

Torre then revealed a year ago that Aspiration — a now-bankrupt tree-planting service that counted Ballmer among its investors — had signed Leonard to a lucrative sponsorship deal in which he reportedly performed no work. The league's investigators claimed that some Aspiration officials initially did not want to hire Leonard but were assured that they would be receiving the money to pay him via additional investment from the Clippers.

According to the NBA's investigatory report, the Clippers also helped arrange for three other companies to negotiate sponsorship deals with Leonard in which he provided little to no actual service.

In addition, the Clippers were found to have covered business expenses for Leonard that he should have paid for himself. That led to Leonard also being fined.

The NBA stripped the Clippers of five first-round draft picks, fined the team $30 million, fined Leonard $700,000 and suspended team governor Steve Ballmer from all league and team activities for one year. Clippers executives Lawrence Frank (six months) and Gillian Zucker (one year) have been suspended without pay. The league also banned Dennis Robertson, Leonard's uncle and former adviser , from conducting NBA business for five years.

The team will be subject to an NBA compliance and monitoring program for five years.

Can the Clippers appeal their punishment through arbitration?

According to multiple reports, there is no way for the Clippers to appeal the NBA's ruling within the league bylaws. The National Basketball Players Association, the players union, could have sent the case to arbitration but has chosen not to fight it. In the league's news release announcing the punishment, the NBA said it has agreed to the punishment terms with the NBPA.

The Clippers could still try to contest the punishment in court, and they appear willing to do so, according to their initial comments . The difficulty of pursuing that path remains to be seen. In Louisiana, at least, there's always a judge willing to hear a case against the NCAA. The Clippers claim Ballmer has already spent $50 million in legal fees on the investigation — and he has billions of dollars more left in his account.

About those draft picks? Which ones exactly are they losing — and can the Pacers get theirs back?

The Clippers are losing first-round draft picks for the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 NBA Drafts. In 2029, the Clippers have their own pick and the Pacers' pick from the Ivica Zubac trade last season. It is the pick from the Pacers that is reportedly being stripped from them. And, no, the Pacers will not benefit from this and get their pick back. ( Sorry, Kevin Pritchard .)

The Clippers are also reportedly set to acquire the Toronto Raptors' 2031 and 2033 first-round picks, in addition to a 2027 pick swap, in the proposed Leonard trade, if it goes through.

Here's what the Clippers' future first-round draft assets look like for the next seven years:

2027: Thunder have option of swapping their first-round pick or Denver Nuggets' top-five protected pick with Clippers' first-rounder; Clippers then have the right to swap what pick they receive with the Toronto Raptors*

2029: own if lands in Nos. 1-3; if it lands in Nos. 4-30, the Philadelphia 76ers can swap their own first-round pick with the Clippers'

*This is contingent on the Clippers and Raptors completing the Leonard trade.

Who is running the Clippers while Ballmer and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank are sidelined?

The Clippers have not publicly announced their replacements, so far choosing to say only that they intend to fight the punishment.

If the suspensions do stay in place, Clippers vice chairman Dennis Wong — who also is the team's alternate governor — presumably would represent the franchise for league business in place of Ballmer.

Ballmer also played an outsized role within the league, serving as one of NBA commissioner Adam Silver's more trusted advisers among owners. He headed the NBA's powerful audit committee and will need to be replaced there.

Frank's six-month suspension will carry past the NBA's Feb. 11 trade deadline, but — unlike Ballmer — the head of basketball ops is expected to be back before the end of the season. The Clippers also just signed Frank to a multiyear extension last season, so it doesn't appear like he will be removed entirely from his role unless Ballmer opts for a complete housecleaning.

In the meantime, the Clippers could choose to delegate the responsibilities to other members of their front office. Trent Redden is the team's general manager and the Clippers have a pair of assistant GMs: Jud Winton and Mark Hughes. Redden, Winton and Hughes were all promoted to their current roles in June 2023.

Will the Clippers-Raptors trade still happen?

According to Leonard himself, the answer is "Yes." In his statement after the punishment was announced, Leonard said: "As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate."

In July, a trade that would send Leonard to Toronto in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, two second-round picks and a pick swap was put on hold due to the ongoing investigation. Now that the punishment has been handed out, with Leonard receiving only a $700,000 fine and his contract not being voided, multiple reports expect the trade to go through in the coming days.

Could the Clippers (or the Raptors) potentially pull out of the trade? Technically, yes, but the Clippers would seemingly have no reason to do so other than spite. They need first-round picks more than ever and they're getting a pair in this deal. Not to mention, welcoming back the player whose free-agent demands led to all of this mess wouldn't seem to go over well with the local fans.

Uncle Dennis is Dennis Robertson. Robertson has served as Leonard's business adviser. He is also Leonard's actual uncle.

Robertson was investigated by the NBA in 2019 over whether he asked teams for impermissible benefits during Leonard's free-agent process. Robertson was accused of asking for part ownership of the team, a private plane to be available to Leonard at all times and a guaranteed amount of off-court endorsement money that could be guaranteed to Leonard if he played for that team, per The Athletic. Ultimately, the league claimed it had no evidence that the Clippers granted illegal benefits to Leonard during his free agency. The team, Leonard and Robertson did not face punishment as a result of the investigation.

This time around, Robertson's name was listed on a contract between Aspiration and KL2 Aspire LLC. The specific sentence pertaining to Robertson specified that all "communication required or permitted under this Agreement" be sent to Robertson. In addition to that, Robertson was listed in the contract as Leonard's "designated representative."

Robertson's name being on legal documents proves he had at least some involvement in the two companies involved in the alleged scandal. While Robertson's name being on documents didn't necessarily prove anything, it gave the NBA evidence to reopen its 2019 investigation into Leonard's free agency and led to his five-year ban.

What is Aspiration, and how did they get involved? What services were they contracting Leonard to perform?

Aspiration was founded in 2013 as an environmentally conscious digital bank. While several notable celebrities and companies partnered with the company over the years, Aspiration signed a $300 million endorsement deal with the Clippers in 2021 and a $28 million deal with Leonard the following year.

In September, Torre reported that Ballmer and the Clippers used Aspiration as a way to circumvent the NBA's salary cap and pay Leonard more money to sign with the team in free agency. The deal with Leonard was reported essentially as a no-show marketing agreement.

Yes. The NBA's investigators said three additional companies — Boingo, Daktronics and Lockton — had similar little-to-no-work sponsorship deals with Leonard that Clippers executives helped cultivate.

According to the report, "Each agreement was signed by a company that had never before [and has never since] signed an endorsement agreement of remotely the same financial magnitude as the one it entered into with Mr. Leonard; and none of the companies has ever signed any other athlete endorser of Mr. Leonard's caliber; each agreement imposed minimal performance obligations on Mr. Leonard relative to the amount he was paid; none of these agreements were publicly announced, defeating the foundational purpose of an endorsement agreement: to obtain associational benefits of the company's relationship with the endorser; and investigators did not uncover or receive evidence reflecting that the companies exercised their rights for meaningful player activation; the record reflects that Mr. Leonard's only confirmed activity under any of the agreements was a visit to a military base on a single occasion under one agreement and signing some memorabilia under another."

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reacts to Making USA's FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Roster, Eyes 2028 LA Olympics Spot
articles.summary: Ahead of her FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup debut for Team USA, Indiana Fever superstar guard Caitlin Clark provided some insight into her mindset this week.
articles.body:
Ahead of her FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup debut for Team USA, Indiana Fever superstar guard Caitlin Clark provided some insight into her mindset this week.

In an interview Wednesday with FIBA's official website , Clark expressed gratitude for the opportunity to represent her country in a major international competition.

"It's crazy, and I think you know, you get used to it," Clark said. "I think at the same time, I almost think about it another way. Like, how lucky am I? This is pretty special and pretty cool, and there's so many people that would kill to be in this spot and have this type of opportunity.

5 reasons women's FIBA World Cup is must-see TV

Lost Passport Keeps Li Out of World Cup 😭

"Especially to play for the USA team, let alone play in the WNBA and live out your dream every single day. So I try to look at, look at it the other way and think about how lucky I am and how grateful I am."

When the last FIBA Women's World Cup was held in 2022, Clark was still playing collegiately at Iowa, and she went on to be named the Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year in both 2023 and 2024 before going first overall to the Fever in the 2024 WNBA draft.

That same year, Clark was considered a strong candidate to be part of the U.S. women's basketball national team at the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris, but she was not selected.

Clark admitted that the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles are on her radar, and she could solidify her standing with a strong showing in the World Cup.

"Obviously getting to watch the games in Paris, like just thinking about how such a cool opportunity that would be to hopefully one day maybe make the Olympic team," Clark said. "And I feel like obviously, we're at the halfway point of, you know, LA in '28.

"Even getting to play here in the World Cup, that's special within itself, too. Sometimes this is an even harder competition than the Olympics. I think one of the most fun parts is the international game and talent is growing and growing. These competitions are only getting harder to win. I think you just wait your turn, continue to put in the work, and your game kind of evolves as you get older."

Already a three-time WNBA All-Star, Clark will look to help Team USA continue its run of FIBA World Cup dominance.

The Americans have won the World Cup each of the past four times it has been held, and six of the past seven times.

The lone exception during that stretch came in 2006 when Australia won it all and the United States had to settle for a bronze medal.

With Clark, Napheesa Collier, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese and a host of other big names leading the way, the U.S. is an overwhelming favorite to win its fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup.

The Americans' gold medal defense will get underway Friday when they face China in their Group D opener in Berlin.

articles.title: Ukrainian center Kate Koval releases statement regarding her departure from LSU women's hoops team
articles.summary: Kate Koval's Instagram statement reveals how Kim Mulkey's signing of Russian center Anna Minaeva drove her away from LSU women's basketball.
articles.body: Ukrainian center and former LSU women's basketball star Kate Koval has broken her silence regarding her departure from the team. Koval announced she was stepping away from the program back in August, with LSU head coach Kim Mulkey citing "personal reasons" as the cause for her center leaving. On Wednesday, Koval released a statement on her official Instagram page, confirming suspicions that her choice to walk away from the Tigers stemmed from Mulkey acquiring 17-year-old Russian center Anna Minaeva. "After much reflection, I have made the difficult decision to step away from the LSU Women’s Basketball program and withdraw from LSU," Koval's statement reads. "At the conclusion of last season, I fully intended to return and continue my collegiate career at LSU. However, in April, several days after the transfer portal had closed, I was informed of the decision to sign a Russian player." RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY Koval goes on to say that her father's service in the Ukrainian Army, along with the deaths and serious injuries of many of her friends and family members because of "Russian aggression," factored into her exit. Mulkey claimed she was only doing what was best for the basketball program when she decided to bring Minaeva into the fold and added that she "cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries." PROFESSIONAL SPORTS AND MEDIA NEED TO STOP ACTING LIKE RUSSIAN ATHLETES ARE PUTIN PUPPETS The LSU head coach reportedly believed she would be able to use Koval and Minaeva as "ambassadors" to help mend geopolitical fences and promote unity through her locker room. "The timing of this situation and the deeply personal effect it has had on me, my family, and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me," Koval added. NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR Despite the sour taste left in her mouth by Mulkey's decision, Koval has made it clear that she still wants to play college basketball for a team during the 2026-27 season. "I hope the NCAA recognizes the circumstances surrounding my situation and understands the seriousness and deep nature of this matter. More than anything, I hope I am given the opportunity to compete at another school during the upcoming 2026–27 basketball season." articles.title: Gillian Zucker was Steve Ballmer's trusted lieutenant. Now she's at the center of the Clippers' Kawhi Leonard scandal
articles.summary: Zucker rose from an unpaid minor-league internship to become one of the most powerful women in sports.
articles.body:
Nine months after the jubilation of finally landing the superstar free agent they believed would transform their franchise, the Los Angeles Clippers were already feeling pressure to keep their prized acquisition happy.

Dennis Robertson , Kawhi Leonard's uncle and business manager, demanded $10 million per year in financial benefits outside the salary cap for his nephew and insisted the Clippers stop dragging their feet in helping obtain it.

At the center of the Clippers' efforts to funnel money to Leonard was the team's top business executive, Gillian Zucker, according to the results of a year-long investigation conducted at the NBA's behest by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Zucker, 57, is a trail-blazing former Triple-A baseball assistant general manager and auto racing executive who in 2014 became Clippers owner Steve Ballmer's first major hire as he sought to revitalize the long-struggling franchise.

Investigators describe Zucker as the intermediary between Robertson and four companies that were already doing business with the Clippers as the organization designed and constructed the $2 billion Intuit Dome. Zucker, the Wachtell report says, "directly initiated, facilitated and induced" Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, Lockton Insurance and, eventually, Aspiration into entering lucrative endorsement agreements with Leonard.

Since investigators found that the Clippers audaciously circumvented salary-cap rules when they courted Leonard in free agency, the NBA handed down the harshest punishment in league history . The Clippers have vehemently denied wrongdoing , calling the investigation "heavily biased" and vowing to fight their $30 million fine and loss of five future first-round picks "through every avenue available to us."

While investigators describe Ballmer, Zucker and president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank as the "three individuals most responsible for the Clippers' rule-breaking," it's Zucker who is portrayed in the harshest light. Her name appears 56 times in the 36-page Wachtell report, more than the 48 times that Frank and Ballmer are mentioned combined.

Each time that Zucker assisted in Leonard landing an endorsement agreement, investigators say she went out of her way to send "introduction" (their quotes) emails meant to provide the Clippers with legal cover. Zucker allegedly made sure the emails were written to make it seem like the relevant company had requested to meet with Leonard, but the Wachtell report found that it was the Clippers who initiated the partnerships as a way to funnel money to Leonard outside the NBA's pay structure.

In spring 2020, Daktronics was competing for the chance to manufacture the Intuit Dome's massive double-sided Halo Board and other video screens inside and outside the venue. The Clippers informed Daktronics that it could secure the project if the company agreed to provide some amount of business back to the team.

"Ms. Zucker thereafter suggested to a Daktronics senior executive that this 'spend back' could be accomplished through an endorsement agreement between Daktronics and Mr. Leonard," the Wachtell report reads. "Daktronics believed that failing to enter into a commercial relationship with Mr. Leonard could jeopardize its ability to win the bid for the Intuit Dome."

Investigators also found that Zucker also sent an "introductory email" connecting Leonard and Aspiration on November 5, 2021, after she had already helped structure an endorsement deal between the parties. That email "was drafted solely for record-making purposes," according to the Wachtell report, "and was not a genuine communication intended to kick off a dealmaking process."

It's not hard to guess why the NBA suspended Zucker without pay for a full year but only stuck Frank with a six-month penalty. Investigators felt that Zucker impeded their progress by providing false or misleading answers.

"Ms. Zucker made several statements that proved inconsistent with contemporaneous documents, other witness statements, and the broader chronology of events, professed a lack of recollection on important issues, placed responsibility on subordinates, and offered inconsistent renditions of facts in separate interviews," the Wachtell report reads. "By contrast, Mr. Frank openly discussed with investigators his conduct from the relevant time period, recalled details of key events, took responsibility for the actions of subordinates, and was generally consistent across his interviews."

The results of the NBA's investigation represent a stunning fall from grace for Zucker, who for years has been ranked among the most influential women in sports. Not bad for a woman whose first job was an unpaid internship with a minor-league hockey team during her senior year at Hamilton College in Clinton, New York.

One of Zucker's first jobs after college was running the concession stands for the Single-A High Desert Mavericks in Adelanto, California. While delivering the commencement address at her alma mater in 2022 , Zucker described what it was like pulling up to the Mavericks' tiny, cinder-block stadium in the Mojave Desert after a cross-country drive.

"My step-mother turned to me and said, 'I hope you didn't just ruin your life,'" Zucker recalled with a chuckle.

Zucker's first big break as a sports executive came in 1998 when International Speedway Corporation, which owned and operated more than a dozen NASCAR racetracks across the country, recruited her to lead the development of a brand-new racetrack in Kansas. She then moved to Daytona before spending nine years in charge of Auto Club Speedway in Fontana, California, the largest racetrack on the West Coast.

The challenge of selling tickets in a non-traditional NASCAR market was one that Zucker never fully solved, but empty seats in the grandstands certainly weren't a result of lack of effort on her part. She improved the fan amenities at the track, tirelessly promoted races and somehow persuaded celebrities like Hilary Duff and Nick Lachey to journey the 50 miles from Hollywood to the Inland Empire.

When Ballmer sought to hire a new president of business operations after buying the Clippers in 2014, he interviewed more than two dozen candidates for the position. Zucker won him over with her boundless enthusiasm, her knowledge of the Southern California market and her innovative approach to marketing.

"What an exciting time to be part of the L.A. Clippers," Zucker said at the time. "There's something special happening in this organization that has captured the attention of Los Angeles, the NBA and the nation. Steve Ballmer's energy and enthusiasm is contagious and inspiring."

Over Zucker's decade-plus with the Clippers, Ballmer entrusted her with rebranding the team, improving the fan experience and managing the design and construction of the $2 billion Intuit Dome. In return, Zucker only seemed to grow more loyal to Ballmer, describing him during her 2022 commencement speech at Hamilton as the "best owner in professional sports" and "one of the best minds in modern business and philanthropy."

"He challenges, he questions, he cajoles," Zucker continued. "But mostly he cares, deeply. He compels us to think critically, imagine boldly and to remember that when we think we've arrived, we're only getting started on the next destination."

In the wake of the NBA's investigation into the Leonard scandal, the next destination for Zucker suddenly is a lot murkier.

"Ms. Zucker acted on Mr. Robertson's demands to help Mr. Leonard achieve lucrative endorsement opportunities," the Wachtell report concludes, "and when interviewed, she made misleading and false statements to investigators about her and the Clippers' role in doing so."

articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers are among the young talents set to represent the United States at the FIBA World Cup, and the Indiana Fever star said she's excited to share the backcourt with her Dallas Wings counterpart.

Team USA's younger core—which Bueckers dubbed the "Young and Turnt" crew back in December—includes that backcourt, alongside Aliyah Boston, Angel Reese, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron. "While they are kind of rookies, in my mind they're veterans," USA Basketball national team director Carol Callan told ESPN's Alexa Philippou about the younger group. articles.title: Tristen Newton's G League rights acquired by Kings, reunites with UConn teammate Alex Karaban
articles.summary: The Houston Rockets waived Tristen Newton last week despite his stellar 2025-26 G League season.
articles.body:
Two years after combining for 25 points and 11 rebounds in a national championship win over Purdue, UConn men's basketball greats Alex Karaban and Tristen Newton have been reunited as NBA teammates.

The Sacramento Kings ' G League affiliate, the Stockton Kings, acquired Newton's returning player rights in a three-team deal Thursday afternoon. Karaban, meanwhile, joined the Sacramento Kings this summer after being selected with the 29th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. The Kings traded up to select him.

Newton spent the 2025-26 season on two-way contracts with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Houston Rockets , appearing in one NBA regular-season game for each team. The 6-foot-5 point guard was released by the Rockets last week despite earning All-G League honors, allowing the team to sign former Providence and George Washington center Rafael Castro.

Leading UConn's offense against Purdue, Newton scored a team-high 20 points to go with seven assists and five rebounds while helping shut down the Boilermakers' backcourt. It was an all-around effort that typified his excellent senior season in Storrs. Newton arrived as a transfer from East Carolina ahead of the 2022-23 season, and his production exploded during the 2023-24 season under Dan Hurley. He averaged 15.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 6.2 assists while becoming the first player in program history to record four triple-doubles.

Newton was among four UConn players selected in the 2024 NBA Draft, heading to Indiana as the No. 49 overall pick. He was waived by the Pacers in January 2025 and later joined the Timberwolves. He has played in nine total NBA games across the past two seasons.

The Texas native earned $321,714 during his half-season with Houston on a two-way contract last season. That was roughly half of the full-season salary for a two-way player. Players signed directly to the G League earn around $40,000 per season, but Newton could sign a more lucrative two-way or Exhibit 10 contract.

Karaban will hope to carve out a role within a rebuilding Kings squad that could sorely use a power forward with his proven perimeter-shooting skill set. Still, recent history suggests that Karaban and Newton will likely spend some time together in Stockton, as each of the last 10 players selected No. 29 overall has made multiple G League appearances.

articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, is easily one of the most talented players in the world. The multi millionaire has tackled every difficult chapter in his life, as his wife, Ayesha Curry, has stood by his side. But things were not always easy for the four time NBA champion.Stephen Curry opens up about the time in his life when he had to tackle a difficult chapter as Ayesha Curry supported himIn an interview with TIME, the star player Stephen Curry opened up about the most difficult phase of his life as he said, “Probably the transition from high school to college. There was a lot of pressure being Dell Curry’s son, growing up in Charlotte, being in ACC country. I was probably really small for an aspiring Division 1 athlete.”The Golden State Warriors' star player added, “And I was looked over by pretty much every non low-D1 school. And it was kind of shock. I was a pretty good high school player, so it was kind of a weird dynamic. I really desperately wanted to play ACC basketball. articles.title: España arranca el Mundial con el podio como objetivo
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina parte como una de las aspirantes a las medallas antes del complicado debut de este viernes (17.45 horas) ante la anfitriona Alemania
articles.summary: La selección femenina parte como una de las aspirantes a las medallas antes del complicado debut de este viernes (17.45 horas) ante la anfitriona Alemania
articles.body: Un día después del 20 aniversario del oro de Saitama, una selección española sueña en el inicio de su camino en otro Mundial. La femenina regresa al campeonato ocho años después. En 2018, al calor de Tenerife, conseguía el bronce, su tercera medalla tras el de 2010 y la plata de 2014. El deseo es volver al podio. Una ambición que parece alcanzable. Por potencial y porque la reciente incorporación de las jugadoras de la WNBA a todas las selecciones deja un torneo muy abierto y con escasas certezas. Ahí, España tiene una ventaja sobre el resto: es un equipo. Las 'americanas' María Conde, Raquel Carrera, Alicia Flórez, Megan Gustafson y Awa Fam deberían sumar a lo mucho y bueno que ya había: Iyana Martín, Mariona Ortiz, Maite Cazorla, Elena Buenavida, Helena Pueyo, Paula Ginzo y la capitana Alba Torrens, única con experiencia en un Mundial y ganadora de las tres medallas antes citadas. A pocas horas del estreno, ya hay mariposas en el estómago. "El equipo no está nervioso, ni ansioso sino expectante. Si no pasa algo por dentro antes de una cita así, nos deberíamos retirar", decía el seleccionador Miguel Méndez, también debutante en un Mundial. "Ni el primer entrenador, ni la jugadora más joven tienen que dar por hecho que van a estar aquí. Tenemos que disfrutar del día a día y competir cada partido", recomienda. "Si disfrutamos van a salir las mejores cosas de nosotras", comparte María Conde. Hace un año, la selección se colgó en el EuroBasket una plata inesperada que bien pudo ser oro, porque se le escurrió de entre los dedos. Ahora, los rivales estarán advertidos. Empezando por la anfitriona Alemania, primer escollo (este viernes, 17.45 horas). Público a favor y el liderazgo de Leo Fiebich, conocida por muchas de las españolas tras pasar por el Casademont Zaragoza y el Valencia Basket. Ahora juega con Carrera en las Nueva York Liberty. Junto a su estelar escolta, las alemanas cuentan con una batería interior de muchos centímetros: Luisa Geiselsoder (1,93 m.), Frida Bühner (1,86 m.) y Nyara Sabally (1,96 m.), compañera de Conde en la Toronto Tempo. Sin embargo, faltará una de sus estrellas, Satou Sabally, que no ha podido recuperarse de un golpe en la cabeza que le ha obligado a decir adiós a la presente temporada. Después de Alemania vendrán Mali (este sábado) y Japón (este lunes). El primero de cada grupo pasa directo a cuartos. Segundos y terceros afrontarán un play-in de octavos con apariencia de campo de minas. Pero el liderato llevaría al lado de Estados Unidos, la gran favorita y el equipo intratable que, sin embargo, esta vez lo parece menos. Soñar es gratis. Y necesario.

articles.title: Awa Fam e Iyana Martín, el aura de la nueva generación: "Nos morimos por ganar"

Todo es natural en dos jugadoras llamadas a marcar una era en el baloncesto español. Con sólo 20 años, serán piezas clave en las aspiraciones de la selección en el Mundial Femenino que arranca este viernes (17.45 horas) frente a la anfitriona Alemania. De aura, tan de moda ahora, van sobradas. De magia, también. "Están tocadas por una varita", dice Alba Torrens, que sabe un poco de baloncesto y de talento. Pregunta. Tan jóvenes y ya importantes con España. Quizás las máximas representantes de esta nueva selección. Awa Fam. Más que sentirme importante, me siento agradecida por estar aquí. Siempre lo decimos y somos muy repetitivas, pero lo que más nos ilusiona es poder representar a la selección española, poder vestir esta camiseta tan jóvenes y estar aquí y sentirnos desde el primer día que llegamos tan bien con el equipo, bien tratadas y acogidas por ellas y por el staff. Iyana Martín. Yo creo que todas somos importantes y es lo especial de este grupo, que no hay personas más o menos importantes, sino que todas nos respetamos y nos tratamos de la misma manera, tanto nosotras como el staff. Eso hace especial y chulo que estemos aquí. P. ¿No sienten un poco de vértigo? Profesionales muy jóvenes, internacionales, elegidas en el draft [tercera Awa y séptima Iyana], la WNBA, este Mundial... Es ir aceptando, ir escuchando a tu familia y amigos e ir conviviendo con ello. A. F. Lo más importante cuando eres joven deportista es rodearte de gente que te ayude, de tu familia, amigos, gente profesional que te ayude a mantenerte siempre humilde. Yo he tenido la suerte de tener gente así alrededor. Las cosas pasan muy rápido, cosas que esperábamos que pasaran, pero al final lo chulo de esto es que nos encanta competir y que nos encanta estar donde estamos. I. M. Todo se resume al baloncesto. Al final del día es básket y eso nos va bien. P. Ahora son muy buenas amigas pero, cuando se conocieron, ¿conectaron rápido? A. F. No. Fue hace siete años, en la U13 y entonces casi ni nos hablamos. I. M. Sí, había dos grupillos y yo estaba en uno y ella en otro. Pero a lo largo de los años nos han ido subiendo a categorías más arriba, U15 y demás, entonces sí que ahí empezamos a conectar. Ahí fue cuando pensé: "Ostras, Iyana Martín. ¡Wow!". I. M. Yo te diría en campeonatos de selecciones, ella con la valenciana y yo con la asturiana. Es que empezamos a subir muy jovencitas con las de un año más y ya fue como: "Awa sabe jugar al baloncesto". P. En categorías de formación y en su primer año con la absoluta han perdido todas las finales con la selección... I. M. Muchas, tío, muchas. Demasiadas. A. F. Creo que es nuestro trauma. Se habla mucho de las medallas y ni hemos empezado. Obviamente, hay que soñar, pero hay que empezar tranquilamente y siendo humildes y respetando a los rivales que tenemos en fase de grupos, que ya va a ser complicado. Y luego, a partir de ahí, soñar. Son jugadoras increíbles, estupendas y top en las Ligas en las que juegan. Todo el mundo las conoce, pero nosotras tenemos algo muy especial: somos un gran equipo. No sé cómo son los demás y tampoco nos centramos en eso. Pero es que nosotras tenemos un equipo que tiene una fuerza de grupo muy grande. El grupo puede ganar muchas cosas. articles.title: The Clippers just lost 5 first-round draft picks as punishment from the Kawhi Leonard scandal. What do they have left?
articles.summary: The Clippers now have decidedly fewer roster-shaping tools when they appeared ready to a take longer-term approach and build through the draft.
articles.body:
The decision by NBA commissioner Adam Silver to take five future first-round draft picks from the Los Angeles Clippers for circumventing the salary cap to help funnel additional income to Kawhi Leonard was obviously the most damaging element of the punishment doled out by the league.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer can stomach a $30 million fine. Teams also rountinely weather executive exits or suspensions. Losing half a decade's worth of draft picks?

The Clippers now have decidedly fewer roster-shaping tools when they appeared ready to take a longer-term approach and build through the draft. The five first-rounders the NBA is taking from them cover the five drafts from 2029-2033. In 2029, the Clippers have their own pick and the Pacers' pick from the Ivica Zubac trade last season. The NBA is taking the Pacers pick, which will not be returned to Indiana.

And yet as harsh as the punishment is, the Clippers aren't completely bereft of assets. If their trade to send Leonard to the Toronto Raptors is completed, the Clippers will acquire the Raptors' 2031 and 2033 first-round picks, in addition to a 2027 pick swap.

Here's what the Clippers' future first-round draft assets look like for the next seven years, contingent on the Toronto trade happening in its current form:

2027: Thunder have option of swapping their first-round pick or Denver Nuggets' top-five protected pick with Clippers' first-rounder; Clippers then have the right to swap what pick they receive with the Toronto Raptors*

2029: own if lands in Nos. 1-3; if it lands in Nos. 4-30, the Philadelphia 76ers can swap their own first-round pick with the Clippers'

Having to swap picks in 2027 and '29 with the Thunder and 76ers, respectively, isn't ideal — but it also isn't nothing, especially with the new lottery reforms dissuading teams from completely bottoming out.

articles.title: Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell reveals how booze helped fuel his legendary 71-point game
articles.summary: Donovan Mitchell revealed on the "Cousins" podcast that a few New Year's drinks preceded his historic 71-point game against the Chicago Bulls.
articles.body: There are certain sports where I think it’s widely believed, if not accepted as a cold, hard fact, that alcohol can improve performance. Hasn't everyone's golf game improved with a little swing oil? However, I didn't think basketball was one of the sports, at least not until Cleveland Cavaliers star Donovan Mitchell revealed that he dropped a cool 71 points back in 2023 with a little help from grandpa's old cough medicine. AMERICAN TENNIS STAR AMANDA ANISIMOVA LEAVES FANS CONVINCED SHE DRANK BEER MID-MATCH WITH MYSTERY BEVERAGE Back on January 2, 2023, Mitchell and the Cavs took on the Chicago Bulls. The two teams ended up in an overtime thriller that the Cavs won 145-134, with Mitchell dropping a career-high 71 in the process. "We played them on New Year’s Eve," Mitchell recalled on the "Cousins" podcast hosted by NBA greats Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady. "Then we had New Year’s in Cleveland. Then we played the next day. Now I will say this. I’ve never drank before a game in my life. It was New Year’s. So I did have a drink — a few drinks — the night before the game." NO SEX FOR 10 WEEKS? CHAMPIONSHIP TEAM'S PLAYOFF STRATEGY RAISES EYEBROWS Hey, many a beer leaguer has done that very thing. In fact, like I said, certain sports benefit from a few pops. Bowling is one, perhaps darts. Hell, I've always argued that part of playing cornhole well is having a beer in your hand for balance. "Never done that in my career," Mitchell said. "Haven’t done it since. So I tell people like that was probably what, you know, allowed me to have the night I had." Mitchell is a professional because if that had happened to most of us, we would’ve thought, "Wait, if a few drinks equal 71 points, then it only makes sense that after many drinks I could be holding up a piece of paper with '100' written on it after the game." articles.title: Enes Kanter Sues WNBA’s Chicago Sky Over Ejection From Game Amid Trans Athlete Controversy
articles.summary: Kanter got into a confrontation with WNBA player Natasha Cloud at a game between the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky.
articles.body:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom sued the Chicago Sky on Thursday, alleging First Amendment violations after he was ejected from one of the team's games following a confrontation with guard Natasha Cloud in which he wore a shirt that defined a woman as an "adult human female."

Kanter, who has mocked and protested the WNBA's gender and inclusion policies in recent weeks, said Thursday he was suing the Chicago Sky after "peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights," referencing the shirt he wore to the game between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever on Aug. 23.

The lawsuit alleges free speech violations and says Kanter was banned indefinitely from Wintrust Arena, arguing Kanter's First Amendment rights are protected because the stadium was financed and built as a public project.

Cloud began shouting and pointing at Kanter after scoring in the third quarter, resulting in Kanter standing up with his arms spread and walking toward Cloud before the two were kept at distance by security.

Kanter was then escorted away from his courtside seat and out of the stadium, saying in a tweet later that night he was booted for "supporting WOMEN!"

Forbes has reached out to the Chicago Sky for comment.

Kanter formally declared himself a WNBA prospect last month in protest against the league's gender policies, arguing he qualified under its "self-identification and inclusion" rules. In doing so, he claimed he did not intend to "mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices." Kanter's protest came after Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham said the WNBA should not allow "biological men," rejecting claims she hates transgender people in an interview with ESPN . There are no openly transgender players in the WNBA. The league's rules state, "Only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA," and do not define "women" or provide criteria about hormone levels or biological sex. The league has not commented on its stance following Cunningham's comments and Kanter's actions, though commissioner Cathy Engelbert said last month the matter would be addressed by team executives.

Ex-NBA player Royce White also said last month he was declaring for the WNBA Draft, telling Fox News, "I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purposes of… professional basketball."

articles.title: Enes Kanter files lawsuit against Sky, city of Chicago after ejection from game over Natasha Cloud confrontation
articles.summary: Sky owner Michael Alter said Kanter Freedom is no longer welcome at home games.
articles.body:
Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a lawsuit against the Chicago Sky, the city of Chicago and the operators of Wintrust Arena over his removal from a WNBA game and subsequent ban from future games, he announced on social media.

The 15-page lawsuit, filed Thursday in the Northern District of Illinois Eastern Division, alleges the defendants violated Kanter Freedom's First Amendment rights while taking action against him.

The incident in question occurred during the Sky's game against the Indiana Fever on Aug. 23 . Kanter Freedom sat courtside while wearing a shirt reading "WOMAN, noun. adult human female," a clear poke at the league over the transgender debate that Fever guard Sophie Cunningham ignited with comments the previous month.

Kanter Freedom had already attempted to garner attention and force action from the WNBA by announcing his eligibility for next year's draft .

It's unclear what was exactly said, but Kanter Freedom got into a heated exchange of words with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, who was held back by teammates and staff while Kanter Freedom began walking toward the court.

Kanter Freedom later argued with security and police before being escorted out of the arena.

Cloud, one the WNBA's most socially outspoken players, posted a statement of support to the transgender community on Threads later that night :

"To every trans kid/person, you are apart of MY community and tribe," she wrote . "You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are, and you will always be protected by me."

Sky owner Michael Alter later announced that Kanter Freedom was no longer welcome at Sky home games until " he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat. "

Via ESPN , Alter also went through the sequence of events that led to Kanter Freedom's ejection:

"I heard him last night, he said, 'Well, I didn't cross the baseline,' as if though that's some magical threshold," Alter said last week. "One reason he didn't cross the baseline was because he was prevented from doing so. But regardless of that, the security people's job is not to wait until a threat intensifies. It's to avoid the threat from happening when [a] perceived threat occurs, and that's exactly what they did.

Kanter Freedom had claimed in a Fox News interview that he gave Sky general manager Jeff Pagliocca, his former trainer, a heads up he would be in attendance, alleging that Pagliocca told him to "enjoy the game."

Alter denied Pagliocca said anything of the sort and that the team did not know Kanter Freedom was attending the game until 3 ½ hours prior, as the purchased tickets were not in his name. He said Kanter Freedom's manager texted Pagliocca and read out the exchange to reporters :

"You've always been fair to me, so I figured you deserved a heads up in advance," Alter read. "Enes and I will be at the Sky Game tonight. Hope you are all well." Pagliocca's response was, "appreciate the text," according to Alter. The suggestion, as the Sky took it, was that they were coming to do more than just watch a game or there would be no need for a "heads up."

articles.title: Kate Koval: Ukrainian quits LSU team after Russian Anna Minaeva joins
articles.summary: Ukrainian Kate Koval says she left Louisiana State University's basketball program because of the team's decision to sign a Russian player.
articles.body:
Ukrainian Kate Koval says she left Louisiana State University's basketball program because of the team's decision to sign a Russian player.

Following the arrival of Anna Minaeva, it was announced that 20-year-old Koval had departed for "personal reasons" after one season.

Koval said Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine was why she stepped away.

"My father serves in the Ukrainian military and takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression," she wrote on Instagram.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract. People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes.

"The timing of this situation and the deep personal effect it has had on me, my family and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me.

"This decision has not been easy. While I understand and respect that roster decisions are a part of college basketball, I have to remain true to myself, my values and my country."

Koval, who was expected to be LSU's starting centre this year, has two years of collegiate eligibility remaining.

The transfer portal has closed, but she said she hopes the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) "recognises the circumstances surrounding my situation and understands the seriousness and deep nature of this matter" and allows her to join a different university for the upcoming season.

Koval said: "I felt I had found a home at LSU, and I am incredibly grateful for my team-mates who became family, as well as my coaches, staff, professors and the entire LSU community.

"I will always cherish the relationships, experiences, and memories I made there."

articles.summary: Los detalles de los partidos de las españolas
articles.body: La selección española femenina de baloncesto inicia su andadura en la Copa del Mundo enfrentándose a la anfitriona Alemania. El equipo nacional regresa al torneo con el objetivo de pelear por las medallas. El esperado estreno de España en el torneo mundialista tendrá lugar este viernes 4 de septiembre. Las jugadoras dirigidas por Miguel Méndez se medirán al combinado alemán a partir de las 17:45 horas en Berlín. Este encuentro inicial supone la prueba más exigente de la primera fase para la selección. Tras medirse a las germanas, el equipo español completará la primera fase enfrentándose este sábado cinco de septiembre a la selección de Mali y cerrará su grupo el lunes siete ante Japón. Liderar la tabla resultará clave para evitar la eliminatoria previa de octavos de final e ingresar directamente a cuartos. La veterana capitana Alba Torrens abandera un grupo que combina juventud y experiencia competitiva para soñar con el metal. Si la selección confirma las buenas sensaciones iniciales, peleará en las semifinales del doce de septiembre antes de la gran final programada para el domingo trece en el Uber Arena. El público podrá seguir el choque completamente en directo a través de la retransmisión televisiva en Teledeporte. Asimismo, los aficionados tendrán la opción de ver el debut online mediante la plataforma gratuita RTVE Play. Tras este partido, el equipo se medirá posteriormente contra las selecciones de Mali y Japón.

articles.title: Kanter presenta una demanda tras su incidente y expulsión por llevar "Mujer: hembra humana adulta"
articles.standfirst: Enes Kanter Freedom demanda a las Chicago Sky por su expulsión y la prohibición de acceso al Wintrust Arena.
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom demanda a las Chicago Sky por su expulsión y la prohibición de acceso al Wintrust Arena.
articles.body: Enes Kanter Freedom, el ex NBA que agitó la polémica trans junto a la "MAGA Barbie" (Sophie Cunningham) y ha presentado su candidatura oficial al draft de la WNBA, ha presentado una demanda contra el equipo Chicago Sky y los propietarios del Wintrust Arena, alegando que se vulneraron sus derechos consagrados en la Primera Enmienda cuando fue expulsado de un partido y vetado para asistir a partidos de la WNBA en dicho recinto. La demanda de 15 páginas de Kanter Freedom se presentó ante el Tribunal de Distrito de los Estados Unidos para el Distrito Norte de Illinois (División Este). Además de las Skay la demanda incluye como demandados a la ciudad de Chicago y a la Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, entidad propietaria y operadora del Wintrust Arena. Kanter Freedom protagonizó un altercado verbal con Natasha Cloud (Sky) durante un partido disputado el 23 de agosto contra las Indiana Fever. El exjugador NBA estaba sentado en primera fila vistiendo una camiseta negra con la inscripción: "WOMAN noun. adult human female (Mujer, sustantivo: hembra humana adulta)". Durante un tiempo muerto, Cloud se dirigió hacia Kanter Freedom y le gritó. Él se puso de pie con los brazos extendidos y dio algunos pasos hacia la pista antes de que el personal de seguridad le cortara el paso y le indicara que debía marcharse. Michael Alter, propietario de las Sky, declaró que Kanter había comenzado a increpar y a dirigirse a Cloud, conocida defensora de los derechos LGBTQ+, en lo que él considera fue un intento de provocarla. "Kanter Freedom nos ha demostrado, de manera inequívoca, que tiene el potencial de representar una amenaza. Que no es capaz de controlarse lo suficiente como para que estemos tranquilos ante la posibilidad de que vuelva a acercarse a la cancha y a las jugadoras. Por ello, no se le permitirá entrar al recinto hasta que demuestre lo contrario", afirmó Alter. Por su parte Enes Kanter Freedom sostiene que "mi camiseta logró lo que al parecer toda la WNBA no pudo: definir a una mujer. Sin amenazas. Sin violencia. Solo biología. Y, aun así, eso requirió una escolta de seguridad". "No tienen por qué estar de acuerdo con mi mensaje, pero no pueden silenciarme por ello. No me dejaré intimidar. No permitiré que me silencien. Seguiré apoyando a las mujeres y defendiendo la libertad de expresión", apuntó.

articles.title: De'Aaron Fox Trade Idea to Get the San Antonio Spurs Championship-Ready
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs are saying all the right things about believing in De'Aaron Fox, reportedly pledging their faith in him and even committing to start him in the upcoming season.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs are saying all the right things about believing in De'Aaron Fox, reportedly pledging their faith in him and even committing to start him in the upcoming season.

But we all saw Fox play like the third-best guard on the team during long stretches of the playoffs, and some intriguing numbers support the notion that the high-priced guard might already be holding the Spurs back from becoming the best version of themselves.

However San Antonio actually feels about Fox, it's never going to come out and bash him publicly or lament the four-year, $222 million extension it gave him—which kicks in this year, by the way. The wiser course would be to keep pumping up Fox's public value while actively looking for a trade to move him out of Harper and Castle's way.

San Antonio Spurs Acquire: Trey Murphy III, Dejounte Murray

New Orleans Pelicans Acquire: De'Aaron Fox, Luke Kornet, 2027 first-round pick (via ATL), 2028 first-round pick (via BOS), 2030 first-round pick, 2031 first-round pick (via SAC), 2027 second-round pick, 2028 second-round pick (NOP's own), 2029 second-round pick (NOP's own)

Fox's Finals struggles aren't enough to justify trading him. He was clearly compromised by the ankle sprain he initially suffered in Game 4 of the Western Conference semifinals. The Spurs don't need to rely solely on what happened last June.

Combine Fox's somewhat injury-related flop, his cap-clogging salary and a larger set of data showing San Antonio is more likely to reach its apex without him, and you've got the more thorough case for moving him.

During the 2025-26 regular season, San Antonio posted a plus-41.9 net rating when Victor Wembanyama played with Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper while Fox sat out. That was significantly better than it performed with Harper and Fox or Castle and Fox while the third member of the guard trio rested.

Some fans like the idea of playing all three guards with Wemby, but those units actually got outscored in a tiny 17-possession sample that also shows the Spurs aren't interested in going that small.

In this deal, San Antonio clears the runway for Harper and Castle to fly, adds a deadly shooter with great size in Murphy and onboards an old friend in Murray who'll be far better suited for third-guard duties than Fox and his $50 million salary.

The cost is high. If the Boston Celtics had to send out two first-rounders while taking back Paul George for Jaylen Brown, the Spurs need to double that pick outlay and throw in three seconds to convince the Pels they should take on Fox's salary and part with Murphy. Murray, coming off injury and on the books for $31 million in 2027-28, is probably not a positive asset in his post-Achilles-tear state.

Critically, San Antonio is only giving up one of its own firsts in the deal.

Murphy is a high-end wing, but Fox was an All-Star last season and would be a veteran first option for a Pelicans team that seems committed to winning this year. That $50 million salary might sting, but New Orleans can bank on more production from him than it was going to get from Murray for $33 million.

Jordan Poole's deal will expire after this season, which should minimize the long-term salary pain.

The real draw here is the draft capital.

San Antonio is sending four first-round picks, three of which come from other teams. The Kings 2031 first-rounder is the juiciest, but it's important that New Orleans is almost entirely getting selections that won't be devalued by San Antonio's likely success in the coming seasons. Two of the three seconds coming to the Pelicans are also their own, which gives them back more control of their draft fate.

Luke Kornet is mostly a salary-matching tool for the Spurs here, even if they'll have to find someone else cheap to back up Wemby. For the Pelicans, though, Kornet immediately becomes the best candidate to start at center. His size, rim-protection and rebounding are all qualities New Orleans' bigs failed to provide last year.

The Pelicans should ask for even more picks while trying to dump other unwanted salary on San Antonio. But if you view this as New Orleans getting three unprotected firsts for Murphy while swapping Murray for Fox, Kornet and another first-rounder, it checks out pretty well.

articles.title: Team USA vs. China Live FIBA Women's World Cup Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: Game Info: USA vs. China | Friday, Sept. 4 | 8:15 a.m. ET | Berlin, Germany
articles.body:
Game Info: USA vs. China | Friday, Sept. 4 | 8:15 a.m. ET | Berlin, Germany

Team USA begins their 2026 Women's Basketball World Cup title defense today against China in a rematch of the 2022 World Cup final. The United States enters the tournament as four-time defending champions and has not lost a World Cup game since falling to Russia in 2006.

However, this year's team looks younger and less experienced than the dominant teams of the past, with six players under 25 and just five players with previous World Cup experience. Veterans Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier and Jackie Young are still playing at an elite level, but the roster also features plenty of rising superstars, including Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Aliyah Boston and Angel Reese.

China will be led by the two tallest players in the tournament: 6'8" Han Xu and 7'3" Zhang Ziyu, who is eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft. They also have dynamic 6'0" guard Shuyu Zang, who averaged 10.6 points and 5.4 assists over five games in the Qualifying Tournament. China will be without one of their best players, though, as Li Yueru will miss the World Cup after her passport was lost in the mail .

Stay tuned for live updates, highlights and analysis throughout the game.
